TITLE: Conditional handover steered by a place-keyed memory of handover outcomes in ultra-dense upper mid-band street networks
ABSTRACT: In ultra-dense street deployments of the upper mid-band, users cross a cell in seconds and blockage changes abruptly at corners and building edges. Conditional handover (CHO) removes the late handover command, but it still executes into cells that the user soon leaves again. We propose MemCHO, a CHO controller that counts, for every 10 m place and direction of travel, how earlier handovers decided there ended, combines these counts with the predicted path of the user, and sets per user and candidate cell both the preparation threshold and the execution offset that the Rel-16 conditional configuration already carries. We evaluated it in a procedure-level system simulation of a street grid at 10 GHz with sites every 50, 100 and 150 m, against A3 handover, a per-user margin rule and CHO, each tuned with the same budget of 48 settings. Over 360 paired runs MemCHO had 19.7% fewer unnecessary handovers and 57.3% fewer failures than tuned CHO (38.0% and 66.9% fewer than tuned A3), and a 1.0% higher delivered rate. It needed 36.1% more prepared cells and 2.2 times as many measurement reports, so our hypothesis of lower preparation overhead was rejected. At equal failure rate the reduction against CHO was 20–29%. The gain grew as the memory filled and disappeared where blockage was not tied to place: in an open area MemCHO had 22.3% more unnecessary handovers than CHO. Handover rates of the simulator agree with ns-3/5G-LENA; failure rates were not calibrated.
HIGHLIGHTS: A place-keyed memory of handover outcomes sets CHO candidates and offsets per user
Against tuned CHO: 20% fewer unnecessary handovers, 57% fewer failures
The price: 36% more prepared cells and 2.2 times the measurement reports
Open area, nothing tied to place: 22% more unnecessary handovers than CHO
All methods tuned with one budget; 2,382 simulation jobs; code and data are public
